facts.rationale: Separates expression width from the explicitly declared backing width.
facts.value: bool(int bit), a read-only indexed predicate over the u8 primary field x0. It constructs a 64-bit shifted mask, but only stored bits 0–7 can test true. Shift counts are unchecked; negative or at-least-64 counts are outside the defined shift domain.

facts.rationale: Corrects the 64-bit storage claim while retaining demonstrated uses.
facts.value: Tests an indexed condition in the eight-bit primary scene-runtime flag field. Observed bit 0 participates in developer update gating, while bit 1 selects versus pause handling and gates item-related behavior; the helper itself assigns no fixed meaning to its index.

facts.rationale: The explicit field declaration overrides inference from neighboring 1ULL expressions.
facts.value: int(void), returning the u8 primary flag field x0 promoted to int without mutation. It is not an interface truncating a u64 backing mask.

facts.rationale: Corrects backing width and distinguishes stored-bit domain from shift-expression domain.
facts.value: void(int bit), an indexed setter for u8 primary flags. The 1ULL shift is evaluated at 64-bit width and the compound assignment stores back to u8. Bits 0–7 are representable; defined shifts 8–63 add no stored bit. There is no shift-count validation.

facts.rationale: Preserves caller-grounded purpose without the incorrect 64-bit word claim.
facts.value: Sets a representable indexed condition in the eight-bit primary scene-runtime flags without disturbing other stored bits. Pause and conditional match-completion/result callers use it to publish scene-wide conditions.

facts.rationale: Removes the false exclusive lifetime claim and preserves alternate writers.
facts.value: For indices 0–7, sets the selected primary bit immediately and idempotently while preserving other stored bits. The loop snapshots but does not consume primary flags. Later writers can change them: the companion clearer clears indexed bits, the developer dispatcher directly toggles bit 0, and loop-state initialization clears x0. Defined shifts above bit 7 do not latch a stored flag.

void(int bit), an indexed clearer for u8 primary flags using ~(1ULL << bit). Representable stored bits are 0–7, not 0–63. Defined shifts 8–63 leave stored flags unchanged; invalid shift counts are not checked.

facts.rationale: Separates the secondary field's declared width from expression width.
facts.value: bool(int bit), a read-only indexed predicate over u8 secondary flags x2. Its 64-bit one-hot expression does not imply 64-bit storage. Only bits 0–7 can test true for defined shifts, and shift counts are unchecked.

facts.rationale: Preserves frame-advance meaning while removing an unconditional single-step guarantee.
facts.value: Tests an indexed secondary scene-control flag. Observed bit 0 carries the developer frame-advance request through pause-related update gates. It grants permission rather than guaranteeing exactly one scene callback: cadence additionally gates on_frame, and secondary clearing occurs only when tracked snapshots differ.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes input recognition, request production and conditional consumption.
facts.value: Supplies the valid-controller Z-edge predicate installed as the default secondary developer-pause callback. While primary bit 0 is set, a successful result sets secondary bit 0 to permit processing through the pause gate. The predicate itself does not advance a frame, and the surrounding protocol does not unconditionally consume the request after exactly one update.

facts.rationale: Restores precise bit tests, per-port behavior and the allocation-failure branch.
facts.value: Scans all controller ports without an err check for its diagnostic chord. Each held-X/triggered-Right match emits diagnostics and either destroys and clears the existing handle or stores a creation result; the optional creation hook runs even if that result is NULL. Multiple ports can toggle repeatedly. A true first callback toggles only x0 bit 0. The second callback is consulted only while that bit is set and can set only x2 bit 0; neither callback result replaces an entire flag byte.

facts.rationale: Separates registration from deferred bit-specific transitions and conditional clearing.
facts.value: Unconditionally replaces both nullable predicate slots without invoking them or changing control flags. Later dispatch toggles primary bit 0 on a true first result and, only while that bit is set, sets secondary bit 0 on a true second result. The loop clears x2 only inside changed-snapshot handling, not unconditionally after one sample.

facts.rationale: Corrects table polarity and identifies the actual predicates.
facts.value: Stores its int argument unchanged in unk_34. Common initialization supplies 0 and match initialization supplies 1. The loop indexes gm_803DA8C8 with this value, ORing the selected entry when cadence 0 is not due and its complement when cadence 1 is not due. Both entries initially equal all ones; the entries themselves are not complementary.

facts.rationale: Preserves observed setup distinction without inventing numeric-state semantics.
facts.value: Participates in common-versus-match runtime configuration through observed values 0 and 1. These values select a table entry used for cadence-dependent scheduler-mask conditioning; source does not establish that they mean disabled/enabled or opposite complementary sides.

facts.rationale: Replaces enabled/disabled terminology with the source-supported index role.
facts.value: Sets the unchecked integer index used to choose one of two u64 entries for scene-loop scheduler-mask conditioning. Demonstrated setup values are 0 and 1; no Boolean normalization or bounds check is performed, and the initial entries are identical rather than complementary.

evidence.why: Cadence flags rather than separate queues.

facts.rationale: Corrects separate-stalled-stream wording and preserves uncertainty about selector meaning.
facts.value: Each call replaces unk_34 with the supplied integer. Common setup writes 0 and match setup writes 1. During updates, false cadence-due flags cause the selected table entry or its complement to be ORed into the working mask. The setter does not modify the table; both initial entries are all ones, so distinct effects of the two setup indices are not established by those initial values.

facts.rationale: Corrects the handle/callback distinction and preserves initialization phases.
facts.value: Runs common initialization without an already-initialized guard. It publishes the GObj creation result even if NULL and attaches the empty process only when non-NULL. It clears one diagnostic-object handle, gm_804D6728, and one callback, gm_804D6724—not two callback pointers. The scene driver installs current-scene context and invokes entry afterward; later loop entry separately clears flags and masks while preserving scene-installed callbacks.

evidence.why: Complete loop, callbacks, counters and exits.

facts.rationale: Replaces the inaccurate all-GObjs update claim with actual mask and lifecycle flow.
facts.value: A borrowed GameSceneInfo pointer is published through gm_804D6720 and supplies opaque enter/exit payload accessors. Separately, the loop resets counters and selected control state, renews queued controller samples, gates controller evaluation and on_frame by update permission and cadence, derives a u64 scheduler suppression mask, services audio and an independently gated nullable stored hook, and invokes GObj scheduling. Scheduling can skip processes according to the mask and process flags. Total-update, active-update and render counters advance at distinct guarded points; reset or exit state 2 bypasses the subsequent render, while normal returning paths wait for XFB flush.
